stories.focus: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers
stories.headline: A governed context layer is more than a vector database
stories.read_scope: Complete product-analysis article: capture, validation, organization, governance and delivery stages; connector upkeep, provenance, ownership, trust scoring, expert escalation, auditability, MCP delivery and vendor-interest caveats.
stories.summary: Stack Overflow divides an enterprise AI context layer into capture, validation, organization, governance and delivery. Its argument is that connectors and retrieval are only the beginning: teams must preserve provenance, ownership, permissions, audit history and changing trust. The article promotes Stack Internal, so its build-versus-buy conclusion should be tested against internal costs and alternatives.
stories.why_it_matters: Inventory one knowledge workflow across all five stages before funding a platform. Measure connector upkeep, stale-answer handling, expert review, permission enforcement and audit needs; then compare those recurring costs with vendor lock-in, migration effort and evidence portability.
stories.image_alt_intent: A five-stage enterprise knowledge pipeline moves from capture through validation, organization and governance to delivery, with provenance, permissions and expert review visible at every handoff.

stories.focus: Applied Generative AI for Knowledge Workers
stories.headline: Independent AI assurance needs visible constraints
stories.read_scope: Complete policy statement: goals, project scope, access and resource limits, redactions, informal pressure, conflicts, financial independence, confidentiality, public methods, iterative reporting, comparability and historical collaborations.
stories.summary: METR explains how external AI-risk work can inform the public without pretending to certify deployment decisions. It commits to disclose project scope, access limits, redactions, constraints and conflicts, while protecting confidential material. The organization also aims to publish evidence and methods for outside analysis, acknowledge scientific uncertainty and issue iterative findings rather than closed-door assurance.
stories.why_it_matters: When reading an AI safety assessment, check who paid, what evaluators could access, which evidence was removed, how methods can be challenged and whether conclusions exceed the scope. These disclosures help leaders distinguish independent evidence from a broad safety endorsement.
stories.image_alt_intent: An external AI assessment report opens into transparent layers for scope, access, redactions, conflicts, methods and uncertainty, allowing readers to trace how each conclusion was produced.
